I never leave reviews, but I want to spare as many people as I can from the pain. Doom is my favorite franchise of all time and Eternal is in my top 5 period. Dark Ages is anti-Doom. It's slow as fuck, vast stretches of maps with no enemies, the parry mechanic is as boring as they could have made it, long corridors of basic zombies to mow down, first level ends with an honest to god stationary turret section that took zero thought or skill and almost made me uninstall, lore/story is so shitty and unnecessary, etc etc. I'm planning on pushing through the whole game through game pass and if it changes my mind, I'll update this review.

In a lot of important aspects this game is a large step back compared to doom 2016 and doom eternal. The battle arenas in doom the dark ages are uninspired garbage. flat boxes of rooms with a shit ton of enemies tossed in there. Inferior soundtrack to doom eternal, and its not even close. the combat is pretty good, but combined with the shitty level design and boring battle areas and boring soundtrack, its just really hard to enjoy this game when i keep thinking of how awesome doom eternal was.
I love that this team keeps trying new things. The loop is different but still tight, addicting, and worth every penny.
Honestly great game, Its sad to see how few people are actually playing this banger of a game right now, But other then that it is fun and feels fresh, I can't wait to see what they do with it

Love This Game So MuCh! a great addition to the DooM Slayers story, Great graphics, Crazy storyline pumping with 200 CC's of FUCK YEA!!! They did a great job with this game and i'm looking forward to the DLC's in the future :)

Played my first and only playthrough on Nightmare and 100% the game in 23 hours.

Forcing a slower paced combat and focusing on parrying with enemies having no clear cut weaknesses sure felt like a downgrade to the chess game Doom Eternal felt like. Unlike it, deaths here felt like they were due to clunkier controls that were simplified for controller's sake, and needing to stand your ground more felt extremely punishing still in a game that very much still holds the philosophy of "Stop moving and you'll die".
Its not to say the combat didn't have its high points though, the lack of clear cut weaknesses allows for more variety in the weapons used, and therefore give the player more freedom in how they want to tackle the challenges ahead, but i have noticed some weapons still creeped miles ahead of other ones where i have barely used some of the weapons outside of unlocking their masteries.

The story is simple, its good, and easilly immerses you in how much of a dedicated badass The Slayer is supposed to be.

The only real complain i have with the levels are that many start with what is essentially just a long tutorial, and the mech or dragon levels are more gimmicky than a mainstay.

As a Doom fan, I would reccommend buying this game for the experience.
If you are only a fan of first person shooters, i would hold off on a sale before buying this game.

I love the setting but this is by far the weakest entry of the three.
Music is rather absent in a lot of places.
Game is much easier compared to the others - even on the hardest difficultly this feels like a cake walk.
I don't play Doom for the story but this one force feeds it the entire game and it is cliche and boring as fuck.
The game relies heavily on the parry/dodge mechanic and the windows to do so are pretty large even turned to the minimum in the settings. Everything you do is in slow mo which is cool the first time then gets old fast with the same animations over and over.
Lastly, optimization was one of the best things of Doom on PC. This is not even near the performance of the old Dooms at their time of release and the hardware they had to run on.

One of my biggest gripes is the Mech and Dragon gameplay feels incredibly shoehorned and rushed so they could hype it up in the trailers. When you play it, instead of feeling like a badass, it feels like an old school Spyro minigame.

For a Doom game. This just screams SAFE. They didn't want to do anything crazy or more controversial than just killing Demons or adding any mechanics that would actually change the game up from its predecessors too much.

Increíble juego de DOOM. Es diferente al Eternal por su diferencia en movilidad pero eso lo compensa con la brutalidad de las armas y el uso del escudo y el cuerpo a cuerpo. Ese cambio me parece buenísimo e innovaron correctamente para darle un toque distinto. Sin embargo, no es mi estilo preferido. Lo siento más como un shooter brutal mas que un FPS frenético como lo que fue el DOOM Eternal. La historia la entendí muchísimo más y se me hizo sorprendentemente interesante. Es un juegazo.

Very Optimized game, stages load fast, plenty of eye candy settings to choose from, runs very fine on my 5090 and 5080 gaming at 4k, gun fight, gun collection and progression is impressive as always, difficulty settings are challenging, agonizing and fun, the collecting/completion goals are very quick and straightforward, the story/lore is rich and deep not your usual DOOM franchise I'd say, I just simply love it as a fan of run-and-gun shooting games, looking forward on the next installment!!

I really like this Doom game. 

I won't pretend this game doesn't have flaws; Its system requirements are quite high due to forced ray-tracing, and compared to past games it's lacking a lot of interesting post-game content.

But it still manages to be a phenomenal game. I really love how they've implemented just straight up Lovecraftian/Cthulhu eldritch monsters alongside Hell. The combat really got made melee combat truly a core part of the gameplay, and the shield is just so freaking fun to use. While the previous two games made me feel powerful, this game's combat really makes me feel like the true warrior that Doomguy has become.

I enjoyed it for what it is but certainly enjoyed Doom Eternal a bit more. 

Also a big miss for not having Mick Gordon on OST but i am certain everyone knows that already.

I can't put my finger on this, but somehow TDA feels, hollow? I don't know if its the lack of glory kills, the ability to parry every single attack in the game, or the fact that there is the complete removal of weapon swapping or ammo management, but this game feels like a step down from 2016, and off a cliff compared to eternal. I am not a fan of "get good" styles of games, but Eternals gameplay was actually perfect. It crushed balls in just the right way too keep anyone hooked, and it was going to be an impossible task to follow that game up and not just rehash the same game again, but they went way too far in the other direction. Beat the story on nightmare my first playthrough, and I died less than 5 times over the 22 levels.

This is not a bad game in any regards (justice for Mick Gordan) but it is by far the weakest game in the series by far. Disappointing for what seems like a sendoff to the series for now.

this was already a great game but on replay everything just clicked more. Insanely fun combat arenas with the best arsenal in the series. Level layout is top notch, and you know what this one the story isn't actually bad, I mean it's not great either but it's at least actually something you can follow along to. Mech levels and dragon levels are fun diversions as well. Revelations is a kick ass expansion with 5 great levels (and a hub level). I really like the end game stuff except the astral boss fight is really janky. Had to lower difficulty from ultra violence for that one as even just falling was killing me pretty easily. Besides that, one blemish this is a stellar game and after putting some thought into it I would put this above Doom 2016 but below Eternal. This is the greatest fps trilogy since Halo 1-3.
Great game, the combat loop, weapons and level design are amazing, 2016 and tda are my favorites from the modern dooms, also, fuck microsoft.

What's incredible about Doom the Dark Ages is that underneath all the parry slop, weapon and upgrade progression there lives an actual beating heart of a game. The game's heart is pumping blood to every organ and appendage with a beat, silence and another beat. Each pulse of gameplay is heavier and more intense than the last one until you get to the last 5 stages or so where the parry party really overstays it's welcome. It's all so tiresome after a while.

Doom 6 (I think) does the shooting and movement right but it's life may be cut short due to heart failure. Parry slop, currency collection, needless systems progression, "exploration" and an abysmal needless story clog it's arteries. The body is in good shape too despite the co-morbidities : 120 fps, native resolution all the way just as God intended. 

Thank the Makyr that it was all assembled well enough to keep me going because at times it felt like I played for way more than 19 hours and thought the game would never end.

7.5/10, wouldn't play again.
Doom series is known for excellent music, graphics and gameplay, and this game is no exception. I'm enjoying this game so much I'll probably play the whole story again.

This was a down grade from Doom Enternal in every way.. Music is worst... monster feel weak. The whole idea of a shield was cool... until it wasn't.. the whole game is using the shield... No multiplayer , no bedroom in space where all your trophies and gun mounts go. No special discs for old doom games, got rid of glory kills. Every secret in the game is mapped out in a way that anyone can %100 percent every map first try. 
Bottom line is... story was kinda lame... dragon / mech stuff... came down to 1 button parry/ + left mouse right mouse... In the end, game was okay at best... I give 6/10.

This is way better than the internet had me beleive, it's not Eternal but it's great fun. The arsenal is OK and the gimmick levels are way more fun than expected. The fun loop is really good and the story is just there in support of the action. However, the NPCs get in the way of the immersion and don't feel part of the world, they're just there, you can't shoot them or push push them around. In the old day this would have been solved in another way, like killing an NPC would result in some sort of Deus Ex Machina plot device killing the player. Today Doom can't be too violent sadly. That said ... great game. Heretic our of ten.

Besides the worse soundtrack, the game is really good and another great entry in the doom franchise. Compared to ADHD Eternal, Dark Ages definitely feels slower, but the Revelations DLC fixes the issue bringing the eternal fast paced gameplay and mechanics into game. If you like Doom Games you will definitely enjoy this one, it is great.
This game is amazing, better than Doom 2016 and Eternal together. At low graphics settings it looks amazing, my laptot (not the best) can afford stable 60 FPS

It provides a super diverse gameplay loop that almost is a fusion between melee centric and FPS style combat, which is pretty uncommon. The game looks phenomenal, the replayability is great due to the custom difficulty sliders and the combat feels ever refreshing. The main downsides I had with it was that the horde mode is not as user friendly as I anticipated (presets would have helped quite a bit) and the giant fight segments were very one dimensional in comparison to the rest of the game. Otherwise, I felt that this was a real cinematic Doom entry that brought it away from the direction that Eternal was heading.

Wasn't sure if i would like the change of gameplay in comparison to Eternal but during the 1st hour of playing i already got hooked.

Graphics are great.
Sound Design and OST is classic DOOM, nothing to complain about.
Gameplay wise, like i mentioned i was suprised to enjoy the parry system and shield combat, it definitely keeps things interesting after replaying Eternal more than 3 times.

Scratching Multiplayer entirely and focusing on the development of the Singleplayer experience was a great decision.

With 22 Chapters in total it took me just a little over 20 hours to 100% the game, find all the secrets in every chapter and complete all the challenges.

The only Cons i have with this game is the flying, which they should have kept out of the game and the secrets have been a tiny bit too easy in my personal opinion.

Overall i totally recommend buying this game, especially for the DOOM and Quake nerds.

Graphics and atmosphere are top-tier, soundtrack hits hard, and every fight feels epic. Definitely one of the best FPS games out there. If you love action-packed shooters, this is a must-play. The negative reviews for this game make me roll my eyes. So many people whining about how the previous two games were "better" (in their opinion).

This game is extremely well made and keeps up with the quality of the previous two. It is not buggy. The graphics and performance are incredible. The gameplay and animations are so fucking smooth. You still get to feel like an absolute badass.

I thoroughly enjoyed Doom 2016 and Doom Eternal. I had a ton of fun playing this one, too. This game is fucking awesome.

While overall not as good as Eternal, Dark Ages brings a cool fantasy aesthetic and is a much easier entry into the franchise. The extra astral boss of the DLC is a unique fight that is really fun. All in all Dark Ages keeps up the extreme badassery of the franchise while a bit slower pace than Eternal.

I'm enjoying this game, the game only issue is sometimes the mission starts and the doom guy is in different location with no context what is going on. The game progression is good and overall happy with it.

Never in my life have I felt so disappointed by a game as good as this. The newest DOOM is a very good game, bordering on great. The weapons are good, soundtrach is good, the core mechanics are well made, but here's the thing, nothing in this game really stands out. The only improvements Bethesda has made over the previous DOOM are in the level design, the stages are much more diverse and more fun to look at than just lava and flesh over and over. Other than that, I loved the shield, throwing and dashing with it feels so good some of the weapons designed for crowd control actually become pointless. Atlas and dragon segments were fun, the story was... Kinda disappointing actually, I'd love for Thira to have some more time to shine but whatever. Now for my main issue with dark ages is...
It became mediocre in its own greatness. It's too polished, too perfect. All weapons are almost perfectly balanced between each other, which sounds like a good thing in theory, but in practice it feels like an anomaly in game design. DOOM: The Dark Ages is a game equivalent of Uncanny Valley, it feels almost too polished, too... Corporate for my liking. With that said, it is still a very good game, I just feel kind of scammed even though I got it half off. Next time a new DOOM is relased, I'm gonna just play through eternal or 2016 again, thanks.

Overall the worst DOOM game that I've ever played:
- Lazy level design: every encounter is either a large field with a few obstacles, or a mid-sized field with no obstacles. Both 2016 and eternal had epic 3D levels to fly around
- Lazy enemy design: little variation in enemy attack patterns and little strategy required to address specific enemies
- Incoherent combat design: minibosses have huge AOE, telegraphs make it childishly easy to parry.
- Overall really disappointing graphics and art design
- Music is not Mick Gordon, and you can tell

This is a disappointing low point in a series we thought could never miss.

I don't usually write reviews, but the dlc for The Dark Ages has to be the best piece of Doom content yet surpassing even Eternal in my opinion. I could've never known that the addition of the spear would overhaul the entire gameplay of this game THAT much. The game goes from the horizontal mayhem of the base game to feeling like a fighter jet that is also a tank. The spear has so much depth and brings back the iconic movement-based gameplay of Eternal, while also combining it with the parry/melee based gameplay of the dark ages. By the end game, using BOTH the spear and the shield in merciless encounters that throw every single demon the game has to offer to test your limits makes the dlc truly a masterpiece and one of the best shooters ever made. I'd also like to add that the music is also a noticeable step up from the already great base game ost, and the end game content is well worth your while and makes up roughly 40% of the dlc content.

conclusion: the game is alright but is genuinely not worth the money every single triple A titles want to get a grip of your wallet but i say wait for a big sale which will happen in the next year probably.

9/10 if it's your first DOOM game. It's rather rare to see a game with so much action, gore, and high quality cinematic without an iota of contrived political correctness in the great 2020s era of gaming. However, comparing to other DOOM games like DOOM:Eternal, it is a HUGE downgrade, I cam only give it 3/10 for a DOOM game. The slayer lost his jumping abilities in this game, which means this "action packed" game is without verticality, and worst of all, you lost your iconic finisher move "Glory Kill" as well. The entire combat revolves around your Captain America style, shield parry QTE, which effectively turns this game into "Guitar Hero", what a joke! You movement is so limited, and the game is much much slowed down (even at 150% game speed), feels like the developers were designing this game for boomers.
Final verdict: 9/10 if this is your first DOOM game, 3/10 if you are a DOOM: Eternal fan who wants extreme maneuvers (you stop moving, you die) and verticality.

Look how they massacred my boy... Doom is basically an on-rails QTE game now, just the key hints are slightly subtler. You see a row of enemies marching with red shields? Press R. An enemy is flashing? Press E. Green projectile? Right click. Almost no aiming or positioning required. Reminds me of another cult classic's dumbed-down version. Do you guys not have chainsaws?
